answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce optical-acoustic distance bounding. Given a challenge nonce, each node flashes an LED lantern and emits a coded chirp as faint as a whisper. Verifiers measure light-to-sound arrival delays to triangulate coordinates and reject co-located clones. Multiplying identities requires separate transceivers at distinct sites, imposing hardware and siting costs. However, a ridge can block line-of-sight flashes and stall verification.
